characterization_methods.key_findings: Hot-rolled (HR) material is dominated by sheaf/lath Bainite (B) with dark blocky patches labelled Fresh Martensite (FM).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Etched with 4% nitric acid ethanol solution.
characterization_methods.purpose: Analyze phase composition and microstructure of the hot-rolled sample (Fig. 2(a)).

characterization_methods.key_findings: HR phase map gives FCC 0 and BCC 1.000; the field is entirely BCC with no retained austenite present.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 20 kV operating voltage; scanning step size 0.2 um; data analyzed with TSL OIM 7.0, indexing both BCC and FCC phases; minimum pixel size 9.
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the phase distribution of the hot-rolled sample (Fig. 3(a)).

characterization_methods.key_findings: HR XRD pattern shows alpha(BCC) reflections (alpha(110), alpha(200), alpha(211), alpha(220)), consistent with a fully BCC structure and no retained austenite.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Accelerating voltage 40 kV, tube current 40 mA, scanning angle range 30°-110°; XRD phase analysis performed on the rolling plane of the sample.
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the phases in the hot-rolled microstructure (Fig. 3(f)).

characterization_methods.key_findings: Ac1 = 705 °C, Ac3 = 950 °C, Bf = 380 °C, Ms = 346 °C (determined using the tangent method).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Cylindrical specimens (10 mm length x 3 mm diameter) extracted from the hot-rolled plates; thermal cycle per Fig. A1(a): heating at 10 °C/s to 200 °C, then 0.01 °C/s to 980 °C, isothermal hold of 300 s at 980 °C, and cooling at -30 °C/s.
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the critical transformation temperatures of the experimental steel using hot-rolled plate specimens.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: A 39 kg low-density steel ingot, with the composition Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si-0.009S-0.009P, was produced via vacuum induction melting.
The ingot was hot forged and cut into billets measuring 90 mm (length) x 70 mm (width) x 40 mm (thickness).
These billets were heated to 1200 °C and held for 60 min.

Hot rolling was carried out on a high-rigidity two-roll mill, beginning at 1100 °C. The process involved six passes with a cumulative reduction rate of 90%, yielding plates with a final thickness of 4 mm. Finish rolling was completed at 880 °C.
Finish rolling was completed at 880 °C, followed by air cooling.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Phase transformation studies using dilatometry; critical temperature range illustrated in Fig. A1.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Cylindrical specimens (10 mm length x 3 mm diameter) extracted from the hot-rolled plates

structures.overall_structure: The hot-rolled microstructure primarily consists of Bainite (B) with a small amount of Fresh Martensite (FM). The phase distribution consists entirely of a BCC structure (FCC 0, BCC 1.000); no retained austenite is present.

unmapped_findings: The process-schematic microstructure-evolution inset in Fig. 1(a) depicts the post-hot-rolling microstructure as a banded lamellar/pearlitic structure (figure_001), whereas the main Results text (b0026) describes the hot-rolled microstructure as Bainite (B) with a small amount of Fresh Martensite (FM).
